outlook.statement: Domestic exploration, offshore development, international expansion, product diversification, and technological innovation will drive growth in the years ahead. The Government of India's approval of Samudra Manthan, the National Offshore Exploration Scheme, with a Phase-I outlay of Rs 84,084 crore for implementation up to FY 2030-31, will generate demand for drilling, casing, connector and production equipment that the Company manufactures.

The Company intends to continue strengthening its position as a technology-driven manufacturer of specialised drilling and oilfield equipment, while expanding its presence in India and international markets, focusing on profitable growth, technological innovation, geographical diversification, operational excellence and financial discipline.

The Company intends to pursue approvals and tenders with other major players in India and India's private exploration majors, and to the international oilfield service providers operating in the country.
Approvals in this industry are neither quick nor certain, and the Company makes no assurance as to their outcome or timing.

Wells are becoming deeper, hotter, and more deviated, requiring equipment that adapts accordingly. The Company invested in cutting-edge manufacturing and design technologies and applies them to products designed for increasingly challenging onshore and offshore conditions.

The Company proposes to engage M/s Oil Drilling Consultancy Services for providing light technical consultancy services in view of its extensive experience, strategic insight and technical expertise, which are expected to support the Company's ongoing business growth and technological advancement initiatives.

The consultancy services will also assist the Company in aligning its international business strategy, integrating research and development initiatives, and adopting global technologies to deliver high-value solutions for the Exploration and Production sector.

Going forward, UDTL remains focused on strengthening its technology portfolio, expanding its premium connection capabilities, developing innovative oilfield solutions and leveraging its manufacturing and engineering strengths to address emerging opportunities in the global oil and gas industry.

The Company remains focused on strengthening its international footprint, deepening relationships with existing customers and identifying new opportunities to support sustainable growth in export markets.

The Company continues to focus on diversifying its product portfolio, services, markets and customer base. Within the Industrial & Engineering segment, the Company is also taking steps to reduce dependence on contract manufacturing by expanding its own product portfolio and strengthening its brand presence.

The outlook for the Indian oil and gas sector is one of rising activity against a persistent structural deficit. Subject to exploration success, Samudra Manthan targets an increase in domestic oil and gas production from approximately 62 million tonnes of oil equivalent to 80 million tonnes annually, and an expansion of the hydrocarbon resource base from 1.6 billion tonnes of oil equivalent to 2.2 billion tonnes, with anticipated reserve accretion of more than 600 million tonnes of oil equivalent. Import dependence is nonetheless expected to remain elevated, since demand growth continues to outpace domestic production.

For the domestic oilfield equipment industry, the implications are favourable and specific. A programme of 60 deepwater exploration wells, rising onshore drilling intensity at the national oil companies and a dedicated allocation for localising critical equipment together point to sustained demand for wellhead assemblies, drilling and casing accessories, gas lift systems and well service equipment.
Management has stated that growing the Company's presence in export markets, while maintaining margin discipline, remains a key focus for the coming year.

At United Drilling Tools Limited (UDTL), we are committed to integrating ESG principles into our business and operations. Our key focus areas include reducing air emissions, conserving water, responsible waste management, employee safety and well-being, and strengthening CSR initiatives in education, healthcare, and community development. During the reporting period, UDTL made progress in water reuse, workplace safety, community engagement, and governance practices. We continue to improve our processes, adopt responsible practices, and work towards creating sustainable long-term value for our stakeholders.

The Board of directors of UDTL in their meeting held on 21.05.2026 have recommended final dividend of 6% i.e. Rs 0.60 per equity share, for the financial year 2025-26, which is subject to the approval of the shareholders in the ensuing annual general meeting.

orders_or_contracts.statement: Subsequent to the close of the financial year, the Company secured significant orders from Oil and Natural Gas Corporation Limited, Vedanta Limited, and Shivganga Drillers Limited covering large outside-diameter casing pipes with multi-start connectors, stabilizers, tubing, pup joints, crossovers, and other specialised products.

Export opportunities secured from Brazil, Russia, Taiwan and Uzbekistan during and following the year. The Brazilian order for casing pipes with multi-start connectors is ultimately destined for Petrobras.

Successfully completed development order for premium tubing and casing pipes for Oil India Limited. 7-inch Premium Production Casing supplied to Oil India Limited under a development order, successfully installed and commissioned in a gas well in Assam.

Under a supply order from Oil India Limited, Duliajan, UDTL delivered 5,000 metres of 7-inch premium production casing. Of that, 4,000 metres were installed and put to use in a gas well at the Lakowa site in Sivasagar, Assam.
Proposed consultancy agreement with M/s Oil Drilling Consultancy Services for technical consultancy and advisory services.
Successfully executed a development order for premium connection casing pipes with multi-start connectors for Oil India Limited at Assam.

This year, it secured orders from Brazil, Venezuela, and Nigeria, while continuing to serve its domestic clients, including a repeat order from Vedanta Limited for tubing, pup joints, crossovers, and accessories.

Commodity price and industry cycle risk: Demand for oilfield equipment is closely correlated with global exploration and production activity, which in turn is driven by crude oil and natural gas prices.
Raw material price risk: The Company's principal raw materials are alloy steel and other specialised metals used to manufacture downhole and surface equipment, whose prices can be volatile.
Competition risk: The Company competes with both larger multinational oilfield service and equipment companies and smaller regional manufacturers.
Regulatory and export compliance risk: Operating across multiple jurisdictions exposes the Company to varying regulatory, safety and export control requirements.

Foreign exchange risk: As export orders form a growing share of the Company's business, the Company is exposed to movements in foreign exchange rates between when an export order is booked and when payment is received.
Instability in oil-rich regions can disrupt market access and supply chains.
Volatile oil prices can impact investment and demand for drilling equipment.
New environmental regulations or policy shifts can affect industry operations and costs.
Growing adoption of renewable energy sources may reduce demand for traditional oil equipment.
Recessions or economic slowdowns can decrease investments in oil exploration and drilling.
Rising competition from both domestic and international manufacturers can impact market share and pricing.
Interruptions in the supply chain can lead to delays and increased costs for manufacturing and delivery.

During FY 2025-26, the Company received notices from BSE Limited and National Stock Exchange of India Limited, vide emails dated November 28, 2025, imposing an aggregate fine of Rs 84,000 for delayed compliance with Regulation 17(1A) of the SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015. The Company submitted a Waiver Application dated December 11, 2025 to the Stock Exchanges seeking waiver of the aforesaid fines. The said Waiver Application was subsequently rejected by the Stock Exchanges vide their respective communications dated May 11, 2026. Thereafter, the Company filed a Review Application with the Stock Exchanges on July 31, 2026 against the rejection of the Waiver Application. The matter is presently under review by the Stock Exchanges.

During FY 2022-23, BSE Limited (BSE) and National Stock Exchange of India Limited (NSE) issued notices imposing fines on the Company for alleged non-compliance with Regulation 21(2) of the SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015. BSE also issued notice(s) imposing fines for alleged non-compliance with Regulation 23(9) of the Listing Regulations. In respect of the aforesaid notices, the Company re-submitted the requisite compliance to BSE on January 14, 2023, along with supporting proof and acknowledgement evidencing the original timely submission, and requested withdrawal of the alleged non-compliance. Thereafter, the Company filed a Waiver Application dated January 20, 2023 with the Stock Exchanges seeking waiver of the aforesaid fines. The Waiver Application was rejected by the Stock Exchanges vide their respective communications dated March 6, 2026. Subsequently, the Company filed a Review Application with the Stock Exchanges on June 5, 2026 against the said rejection. The matter is presently under review by the Stock Exchanges.
